scope: Symmetric tight-clock Fmax comparison across IHP SG13G2 (25 ns / 20 ns), SKY130A (40 ns), and GF180MCU D (65 ns). All tight-clock SDCs scale I/O delays proportionally (10% in_max, 5% in_min, 5% out_max, 0% out_min). Runtime numbers are single-run isolated-CPU observations (4 E-cores on IHP, 2 E-cores on GF180/SKY130, 4 GiB / 0 swap), not 3-block quiet-host confirmations.

ihp.note: Original 100 ns constraints.sdc had fixed output_delay=5.0 ns, making r227->observe_valid_o cap Fmax at ~43.4 MHz even when internal reg2reg logic ran at 45.0 MHz.

simulation_failure_diagnosis.summary: The post-PNR netlist IS logically/functionally correct (both its 06-yosys-synthesis netlist and the final netlist with its 285 pure-identity CTS buffers collapsed PASS tb.sv at 1369000 ps). In signoff_layout.py's zero-delay '-DFUNCTIONAL' simulation without SDF, OpenROAD CTS inserted an 18-stage clkbuf_16 delay chain (delaybuf_32_clk_i..delaybuf_49_clk_i -> clkbuf_regs_0_clk_i -> 2 buffers, 21 gates total, 9.79 ns real delay) on clk_i_regs to match u_cpu.clk's 8-gate / 8.89 ns latency (inflated by a buf_1 at the clock-gate root _20411_ taking 2.46 ns). On launch FF _31209_ -> capture FF _31287_ (d_valid), data traverses 4 combinational gates (delta 8+4=12), arriving 9 Verilog delta cycles BEFORE _31287_/CLK fires at delta 21 -> zero-delay shoot-through at cycle 6 hangs Ibex LSU. In real silicon (OpenSTA with SPEF), _31209_ -> _31287_ hold slack is +3.59 ns (MET). However, that same 9.8 ns CTS latency DOES cause genuine silicon hold failure (-0.228 ns on prog_be_i[1] -> u_imem1/WEN[7] even after 10 series hold buffers) plus 107 SS DRVs.

ihp-librelane-25ns-delay0.reason: Pass 1 DRT took 48m13s; antenna diode insertion triggered pass 2 which stuck on 1 Metal2 spacing violation at iter 19 and hit 4500s wall timeout.

gf180-librelane-65ns-delay4.reason: DPL-0036: 2 instances (_17763_, _16211_) failed diamond placement search after [GPL-0302] Target density 0.4500 is too low (min feasible 0.50). Resolved by PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT=60 in gf180-librelane-65ns-delay4-d60.

engine_and_composer_gaps.summary: rustsys synth --timing-period <T> hard-rejects any macro-bearing design ('synthesis electrical optimization does not yet model opaque macro buses').
engine_and_composer_gaps.impact: Blocks clock-period-aware carry planning, cover alternative refinement, state/polarity folding, and load-aware cell sizing on Ibex (and any SRAM/macro SoC). Forces tight-clock RustSys runs to fall back to period-agnostic '--goal delay' without electrical optimization.

engine_and_composer_gaps.summary: rustsys opt-timing fails on macro-bearing designs ('no electrical model for RM_IHPSG13_1P_1024x32_c2_bm_bist').
engine_and_composer_gaps.impact: Prevents standalone pre-placement timing/buffering optimization via 'rustsys opt-timing' on SRAM-bearing designs even when SRAM .lib timing models are supplied.

engine_and_composer_gaps.summary: --effort high --delay-relax 0.0 degrades post-route SS Fmax on BOTH PDKs (-0.94 MHz on IHP: 44.05 vs 45.00 MHz; -0.97 MHz on GF180: 13.68 vs 14.65 MHz) while bloating stdcell area (+3.0% IHP, +6.9% GF180) and power (+18.6% IHP vectorless, +6.4% GF180).
engine_and_composer_gaps.impact: Without load-aware electrical optimization (--timing-period), zero-relaxation delay mapping chases zero-load intrinsic pin delay and creates heavier fanout/capacitance loads.

engine_and_composer_gaps.summary: estimated_hold checks chip-global worst_setup instead of per-endpoint end_setup[end], aborting tight-clock builds on unrelated endpoints with huge setup margin (e.g. r531/D with +22.46 ns setup slack) or already-positive hold slack (r96/D with +0.068 ns).
engine_and_composer_gaps.impact: Stock RustEDA flow cannot even finish fe_eco_hold at 25 ns or 20 ns on IHP. Clean ~10-line per-endpoint fix verified in tight-clock/patches/native_ecos.py.

engine_and_composer_gaps.component: Backend setup-timing sizing ECO & selection.json fanout buffer floor
engine_and_composer_gaps.summary: Neither native_ecos.py nor rustroad performs post-placement/post-route setup-driven cell upsizing or buffering, and default selection.json allows weak BUFX1/buf_1 drivers in fanout/delay paths.
engine_and_composer_gaps.impact: On IHP 25 ns, a single AOI221X1 (g2855) accounts for 2.69 ns on the critical path even though AOI221X3 is in the library, and simply raising selection.json's fanout buffer floor from BUFX1 to BUFX3 yielded a free +9.93% Fmax gain (45.00 -> 49.46 MHz), -28 um^2 area, +0.24% VCD power, and 9/9 signoff PASS. Adding targeted setup cell upsizing ECO should push RustEDA comfortably past 52+ MHz on IHP and >16 MHz on GF180 without LibreLane's 2x power / 13.5x runtime penalty.
Need to expose optional 'effort', 'delay_relax', 'timing_period', 'electrical_corners', and optional 'opt_timing' stage in native_frontend.py once GAP-1/GAP-2 are implemented.
